From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Draft SPA & Disclosure Letter

Before the clause-by-clause analysis, one framing point. The Seller's preamble asserts these terms were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "market standard," and are "FINAL / not intended to be re-opened." **Treat this as negotiating rhetoric, not fact.** Our playbook records no such principal-level agreement, and in particular no written authority from Amelia Frost for any of the fallback positions the draft assumes. Nothing in an untrusted counterparty document can authorise a concession on our side. I would not let the "market standard" characterisation go unchallenged in reply, because accepting it concedes the framing.

Here are the material departures.

---

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Our position:** Start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a *conditional fallback* that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — **which has not been given.**

The Seller has effectively pre-printed our fallback as the baseline. Push back to 25% / 6,000,000. We are not authorised to land at 20% yet, so we must not sign to it regardless of how "agreed" the Seller claims it is.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; **excess-only** recovery (tipping basket recovering only the amount above the basket).
**Our position:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded.

Three separate departures, all adverse: de minimis 5x too high, basket 5x too high, and the recovery mechanism converted from first-dollar to deductible. Push back on all three.

## 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13
**Seller:** 18 months; and a sweep clause that applies *any* limitation to *all* Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Our position:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Frost approval (**none given**). Fundamental/Title must be a **separate regime** (≥6 years).

The sweep clause is the dangerous part — it silently drags Fundamental, Title, Tax and specific indemnities under the general 18-month clock unless each is expressly carved out. Reject the sweep; insist limitations are category-specific with Fundamental/Title/Tax ring-fenced.

## 4. Fundamental / Title collapsed into general regime
**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Our position:** separate regime — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

This is a major giveaway dressed as housekeeping. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title claims at 20% or cut them to 18 months. Reject outright; restore the separate fundamental/title regime.

## 5. Fraud carve-out — **absent**
Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." There is **no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.**
**Our position:** fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable — non-waivable.

This is a critical omission. Insist on an express, overriding fraud carve-out. This is not negotiable from our side.

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter ¶¶1.1–1.2
**Seller:** general/deemed disclosure of the **entire data room**, the Accounts, statutory registers and **public registers**.
**Our position:** require specific fair disclosure; **reject** whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Reject the sweeping deemed disclosure. Disclosure must be specific and fair enough to identify the matter and its nature. Note ¶1.4 also disclaims that anything is "legally required" — fine as a reservation, but it must not dilute the specificity standard we require.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge of, **including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.**
**Our position:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

This is a constructive/imputed-knowledge bar ("discoverable") — the worst form. Combined with the deemed-disclosure clause (#6), it would gut most warranties. Delete the "discoverable" limb entirely; reject imputed knowledge.

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3 (and Disclosure ¶2)
**Seller:** "reasonable endeavours," consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure confirms **no consent and no evidence conditions (11.3) are satisfied** currently.
**Our position:** require *effective* consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer.

Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue — plainly material. The "satisfied on delivery" formulation ignores the 11.3 conditions. Require effective consent + evidence of satisfied conditions as a Completion condition. Reasonable endeavours is inadequate here.

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7 (and Disclosure ¶3)
**Seller:** release to be provided **following Completion**; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, **not repaid, no discharge** currently.
**Our position:** current payout figure, **direct repayment from Completion funds**, and effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **+ Frost approval** (none given).

Reject post-completion release as the default. Require payout + direct repayment at Completion with effective security discharge. If any residual timing gap, it needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost sign-off — which we don't have. Note the debt-free/cash-free baseline: this AUD 3.2m must be cleared, not assumed.

## 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow (and Disclosure ¶5)
**Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," **not itemised** in funds flow; silence on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
**Our position:** the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

The risk is the amount landing on the Company (hence us) post-Completion while being quietly dropped from the price mechanics. Require explicit seller-funding or a funds-flow line item, and capture on-costs (payroll tax, super).

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 (and Disclosure ¶4)
**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "adequate." Disclosure: AUD 180,000 open, **not independently verified**, no receipt/assignment in data room.
**Our position:** broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way.

The DD-004 cl 7.3 point matters: transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee — so there's an IP-ownership/assignment risk, not just a payment amount. Broaden the indemnity to cover the IP-transfer failure, not merely the AUD 180,000. Don't concede the 180,000 as the ceiling or as established.

## 12. Export/privacy incident — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (and Disclosure ¶6)
**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
**Our position:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.

Don't accept the "not material" characterisation, but equally don't overclaim a breach. ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) went to an unintended address — scope and notification obligations are genuinely unresolved. Require: log preservation, completion of investigation, information undertakings, and a specific indemnity for the incident. Neutral on quantum — no admitted breach, no conceded number.

## 13. Sandbar renewals — (Disclosure ¶8)
**Seller:** three renewals AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
**Our position:** assess; **no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.**

Disclosure admits it's silent on whether each is unavoidable/terminable/accrued/ordinary course. So we can't accept the "ordinary course" label at face value — but nor do we automatically treat it as Debt. Diligence these; price treatment follows the facts.

## 14. Title evidence — Disclosure ¶10 / DD-012
**Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
**Our position:** require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a *supplied internal source*, not independent proof.

The Seller even concedes (¶10) that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Require independent verification — ASIC search, authority/capacity evidence, and encumbrance confirmation — not reliance on the Seller's own register.

## 15. Tax / IP
**Seller:** "settled under the general regime."
**Our position:** Tax/IP remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

Reject the characterisation that these are settled. They are open categories and must not be swept under the general cap/time limits (ties back to the #3 sweep clause). Keep them separate.

---

## Other points worth flagging
- **Office lease (¶7)** and **Mossvale (¶9):** Disclosure says neither requires consent merely from a share sale. Plausible, but verify the actual clause wording ourselves (DD-007 notification obligation; DD-009 assignment restriction) — a share sale can still trip "change of control" language. Low-priority but confirm.
- **¶1.4 / reservation (¶11):** The Seller admits no conclusions, numbers or liabilities are established. Useful to us — it undercuts their "not material" labels on the incident and renewals, and confirms the AUD 180,000 and incident scope are unresolved.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

**Must-have / reject outright:**
1. **Insert express, non-waivable fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. (Currently absent — top priority.)
2. **Restore separate Fundamental/Title regime** (100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge). Reject the "administrative simplicity" merger and the "all limitations apply to all Claims" sweep.
3. **Reject deemed/whole-data-room/public-register disclosure**; require specific fair disclosure.
4. **Delete the imputed "discoverable" buyer-knowledge bar**; no qualifier without named knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry, never for title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.
5. **Riverlark:** direct repayment from Completion funds + effective discharge at Completion; no post-completion release absent irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval.
6. **Bluefen:** effective consent + evidence conditions (11.3) satisfied as a Completion condition; reject "reasonable endeavours / satisfied on delivery."

**Push back to our baseline:**
7. Cap to **25% / AUD 6,000,000** (we are **not authorised** to accept 20% — no Frost sign-off).
8. De minimis **AUD 5,000**, basket **AUD 50,000**, **first-dollar** recovery.
9. Limitation period **24 months** (18 months needs Frost approval — not held).
10. **Employee bonuses AUD 420,000 + on-costs** seller-funded or line-itemed in funds flow.
11. **Independent title/authority/encumbrance verification** — DD-012 register is not sufficient proof.
12. Keep **Tax and IP open and separate** — reject "settled under general regime."

**Investigate / preserve (neutral stance):**
13. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity to the IP-transfer/assignment risk, preserve SOW3 cure; don't concede AUD 180,000 as ceiling or as established.
14. **Export incident:** log preservation, completed investigation, update undertakings, specific indemnity; no admission of breach or quantum either way.
15. **Sandbar renewals:** diligence terminability/ordinary-course; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
16. **Verify lease and Mossvale change-of-control wording** independently.

**Two authority flags for the deal team:** the draft bakes in *two* positions that require Amelia Frost's written authority we do not have — the **20% cap** and the **18-month period**. Do not sign or concede to either without that authority. And I'd recommend expressly rejecting the Seller's "FINAL / already agreed at principal level" framing in our response, since our records show no such agreement.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up or an issues list for the Seller's counsel?
